exposure: time consumed to reach the health facility
counseled about the benefit of long-acting reversible contraceptives
cohort: The study included 227 reproductive-age women from Butajira town, Central Ethiopia, selected using a systematic random sampling method.
finding: The discontinuation rate of long-acting reversible contraceptives was 22.5%, primarily due to side effects (menstrual disruption), and was predicted by time to health facility, desire for more children, and insufficient counseling about LARC benefits.
